transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, it's... I guess it's mainly what's been happening at night. You see, I'm not working right now, so my schedule is a bit all over the place, but my wife, she goes to bed around 10 or 10:30. And once she goes upstairs—she's a really heavy sleeper, so once she's out, she's out for the night—I usually just stay up watching TV. But then I always find myself wandering into the kitchen. 

And the thing is, I start eating, but it's... it's way, way past a normal plate of food. It's actually gotten completely out of hand. Like, if we have event leftovers in the fridge, which we usually do because we have people over a lot, I'll just start pulling all of it out. I'll get into the fried chicken, the mac and cheese, the sweet potatoes, all the leftover dinner rolls... and I just keep going. I'll tell myself I just want one piece or a little taste, but then I'm eating piece after piece of chicken, scooping out massive portions of the mac and cheese, sometimes not even bothering to get a proper plate, just standing right there in the kitchen. And I just keep eating and eating all of it until a whole catering tray is completely empty, or honestly, until half the fridge is just... gone. It's just gone, and I do it almost every single night. That's really why I'm here.
Do you feel upset or distressed about this nighttime eating? Has it affected your daily life or relationships in any way?

Oh, distressed doesn't even begin to cover it. I mean, yes, absolutely, I feel incredibly upset about it. It's... it's this heavy, sinking feeling every single morning when I wake up and remember what I did the night before, and then I have to go into the kitchen and see the empty containers or the trash can full of wrappers. It just eats away at me, no pun intended. 

And as for how it's affecting my life... well, it's really starting to take a toll. You see, I used to be so involved in our neighborhood. We have this community association, and I was always the one organizing the block parties, the holiday gatherings, the summer barbecues. I loved doing it, and my wife and I were always hosting the planning meetings at our house. That's why we always have so many catering trays and leftovers around, actually. 

But lately... I just can't do it anymore. I've completely pulled back from all the community planning meetings. I've stopped volunteering to help with the events. I just... I feel so embarrassed all the time. I feel like this huge fraud. Here I am, supposed to be this organized, put-together guy running these community events, and behind closed doors, I'm completely out of control, just gorging myself in the middle of the night. 

It's also just so physically and emotionally draining. By the time the afternoon rolls around, I'm exhausted from the guilt and the physical toll of eating that much food so late. And honestly, I'm just terrified that people are going to look at me and somehow know. I'm afraid they'll notice I've gained weight, or they'll see how tired I am, and they'll realize that I'm not holding things together the way I used to. I've even been avoiding some of my closest friends in the neighborhood because I just don't want to have to put on a happy face and pretend everything is fine when it's really, really not. So yeah, it's definitely affecting my daily life in a huge way. I just feel like I'm hiding all the time now.
